To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the emergence of flexible information routing in neuronal networks is a generic phenomenon that is determined by the intrinsic firing rate across neurons.

(i) a high frequency neuron can be a functional hub in a network of low frequency neurons, (ii) the high frequency neuron can control the direction of information flow, (iii) the high frequency neurons can be identified by the presence of a large number of incoming synapses, and (iv) the mechanism is generic and works for networks with more complex topologies.
the firing rate of a neuron is a tunable variable that determines its functional role in a network and the emergence of a directed flow of information.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the fundamental question of how a simple mechanism, such as firing rate, can be used to establish effective information channels in neuronal networks and to control the direction of signal transmission.
the question of how the intrinsic firing rate can determine effective connectivity in a network of neurons.
a fundamental question in brain networks: How does the emergence of flexible information routes occur?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the firing rate of a neuron is a fundamental determinant for the directionality of information transmission in a network.
the emergence of directionality in a network of identical neurons can be controlled by changing the intrinsic firing rate of a single neuron.
the firing rate of a node can determine its effective connectivity, thus allowing the network to dynamically reconfigure its information routing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the firing rate is a parameter that can be tuned to control signal transmission and to establish preferred routes in neuronal networks.
the intrinsic firing rate across neurons may determine preferred routes for information transmission in neuronal circuits.
a high frequency node in a neuronal network can act as a functional hub by establishing a preferred direction of information flow and by increasing the reliability of signal transfer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the firing rate is a fundamental mechanism to control the effective connectivity of neuronal networks.
the intrinsic firing rate of neurons can be used to establish preferential information channels that are robust to noise.
the firing rate can be used to tune the direction of signal transmission in a network.
